steps.title: Why it is hard: the obvious fixes do not hold, and it depends on the model

items.text: The one-line fix, num_keep (keep the system prompt) at 4096: 30.0% wrong, down from 42.0% but still above 11.3% at the default window
items.label: measured

items.text: Client-side trimming has a side effect: qwen3:14b called the logging tool in 24/25/25 of 40 turns per seed with trimming, 40/40/40 of 40 without. Trimming removes the earlier turns that showed the two-call pattern the model imitates (interpretation in docs/FINDINGS.md)
items.label: measured

items.text: Rule loss at 4096 depends on the model: llama3.1:8b 5/5, qwen3:14b 4/5, qwen3:8b 1/5 sessions
items.label: measured

items.text: Larger models at 4096: qwen3:32b 2/3, llama3.3:70b 0/3 (resists rule loss), mistral-small3.2:24b 0/3 (resists rule loss) sessions
items.label: measured

steps.title: The tool: pick a device and a model, get the measured setting

items.text: Each setting carries its label: measured, pending flash-attention control, or not measured. Where we have no data, it says so. Try evo-t2s Intel CPU next.

steps.title: The money: a whole task in the cloud is not cheap, and the failure is silent

items.text: One long agent task (nebius-rebench-openhands, median 62 steps) sent whole to the cloud: USD 1.54 median, USD 2.63 p90 on claude-sonnet-5-5 at an assumed 70% cache hit rate; USD 0.08 on claude-haiku-5-5
items.label: priced, not executed

items.text: Cost to fix a wrong answer: being measured
items.label: being measured

items.text: Takeaway: sending every long task to the cloud is not cheap; escalating only the step that went wrong needs to know which step went wrong, and the failure is silent.

items.text: The local model (qwen3:14b, 4096 window) set duration_min = 60; the standing instruction gives 50. HTTP error: no.
items.label: measured
